input.question: When did straight white teeth become a status symbol?
input.ground_truth: I'm guessing this is a thing in the States? As with so many things, it probably started to become a status symbol as soon as famous people started doing it. This being said, the super white teeth American TV stars and politicians tend to have is not really a thing here in Europe (is this changing?). So it's not a status symbol everywhere. Even teeth you take very good care of should have a slightly yellow tint to them. It's the natural color of the teeth. By making them completely white you're making them look like something that isn't the color of teeth.

Okay! Imagine a long, long time ago, people didn’t care much about how their teeth looked. Some people had straight teeth, some had crooked teeth, and that was okay.

But as time went on, some people started thinking that straight and white teeth looked really nice. They thought it made people look healthy and clean. Also, in old movies and pictures, people with straight, white teeth often looked like heroes or important people.

So, over many years, having straight, white teeth became something that made people look fancy and important. It became a "status symbol," which means it showed that someone was special or cared a lot about how they looked.

But really, everyone’s teeth are different, and what matters most is taking care of them and being healthy!
